purpose: Two fetch calls to Vault Transit carried no timeout, on the path that encrypts and decrypts personal data. encryptFields and decryptFields walk their fields sequentially, so one unreachable Vault holds a request forever, and on Node's single event loop that exhausts the request pool without Vault ever returning an error. This pass bounds both calls and installs a ratchet so a future outbound call cannot be added unbounded. It flips no ASVS verdict and does not claim one: V13.1.3 asks for a documented resource-management strategy across every dependency, and bounding outbound HTTP is one part of that, not the whole of it. Claiming the requirement on this evidence would be the substitution this programme forbids.
requiredInvariants: The bound is a real abort, not a decorative option. The spec reads the AbortSignal the service actually passed and waits for it to fire; a `timeout:` key that fetch ignores is explicitly rejected by the gate.

The measurement is by balanced parentheses, not by a window of lines. A fixed window truncates a long call and reports a bounded call as unbounded - the first version of this scan did exactly that to two Qwen calls whose `signal` sat one line past the window, and the error is recorded here rather than quietly fixed.
The scan's own file discovery is cross-checked against an independent grep in the test suite, so a pathspec that silently drops files cannot report a clean tree.
The gate is anchored on apps/api/src. apps/web outbound calls are a different risk class - browser and server calls to this platform's own API - and are not claimed, not counted, and not touched.
The development stub path must stay free of any outbound call; the spec fails if the stub ever reaches the network.
No ASVS verdict is claimed. The matrix was rebuilt on this head and diffed: zero verdict changes, statusCounts identical. This is a defect fix and a ratchet, not a compliance movement.
No dependency, schema, migration, RLS or policy change. No registration, 1C, marketing or presentation code. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Measured before changing anything: 12 outbound fetch sites exist in apps/api/src across 570 tracked files; 10 were bounded and 2 were not, both in vault-transit.service.ts. An independent grep counts the same 12.
Both Vault calls are bounded at 5 s. Re-scan after the fix: 12 sites, 12 bounded, 0 unbounded.
The gate is proven by reverting the real fix: removing one of the two bounds turns the gate red (exit 1, naming the exact file and line) and turns the suite red.
The runtime spec is proven the same way: removing the encrypt bound fails 'bounds the encrypt call with a signal that actually aborts' while the other three still pass, so the failure localises.
The spec asserts the abort actually fires rather than that the property exists, and it asserts an aborted request surfaces as a rejection rather than a resolved value.
ASVS matrix rebuilt on this head and diffed against main: 0 verdict changes; PASS 129, FAIL 90, NOT_APPLICABLE 88, NOT_ASSESSED 38 unchanged.
scripts/security suite 151/151 green; web-unit coverage gate green; sbom-scan.yml parses and runs the new gate.
